study.question: Can a purchase-plus-one-auxiliary context-update route preserve the full route benefit, and which pair or three-way optimization interaction explains the grouped result? Observed at the same frozen seed: A000=0.6678548720585206, A110=0.6679415531643654, A001=0.6675472255081946, A111=0.6684156159937658, where C,F,B mean enabling each task loss gradient into the shared context embedding through its task-specific product branch. Purchase effect is -0.00030764655 without C/F and +0.00047406283 with C/F; grouped interaction is +0.00078170938. These four cells cannot identify cart versus favorite or distinguish pair interactions from a three-way dependence. Full-route gain over no-route is concentrated in existing longer-history bins (AUC changes about+0.0006784 for17..64 and+0.0008124 for>64, versus+0.0000895 for1..16). These are exploratory observations, not new confirmatory tests.
study.hypothesis: The signed, task-specific context/history product learns compatible shared-context updates from purchase together with at least one of cart or favorite; a pair-specific correction to purchase-only updates may preserve most of the full-route click ranking benefit. Completing the three binary source factors can falsify pair sufficiency and distinguish pairwise from residual three-way dependence at fixed forward capacity. This is a local optimization hypothesis; gradient alignment, general novelty, population causal complementarity and repeated support are unverified.

study.proposed_difference: Submit product_cart_buy(101), product_fav_buy(011), product_cart_only(100), product_fav_only(010). All modules are standalone and differ only in aux_product_context_tasks and matching default; no parameter, buffer, RNG, forward arithmetic, historical feedback membership, task prediction or loss population is added or removed. Existing A000,A110,A001,A111 are reused only under the exact protocol/source/config match. Gates depend on static task identity, never a current/future label value. predictions: Pair-sufficiency hypothesis: max(A101,A011)>A001, and at least one pair reaches A111-0.00015 or better. Absolute0.00015 AUC is a predeclared practical tolerance, not a statistical threshold. No specific winning pair is preselected.
Report I_CB|F0=A101-A100-A001+A000, I_FB|C0=A011-A010-A001+A000, and I_CF|B0=A110-A100-A010+A000. Report every main/simple effect rather than selecting only the positive pair.

Report I_CFB=A111-A110-A101-A011+A100+A010+A001-A000. Verify algebraic decomposition A111-A110-A001+A000 = I_CB|F0+I_FB|C0+I_CFB. These are AUC-scale optimization contrasts, not direct gradient measurements.

At copied common nonzero parameters and buffers, all eight gates must have equal forward predictions and native Dice state updates. Only selected auxiliary product-context embedding Jacobians change. Inactive task heads and projections must still receive their own training-loss gradients.

Expected parameter counts equal32192421 for all new cells; inference computation is unchanged. Full measured training cost may differ in backward graph work. No efficiency benefit follows from an equal-capacity design alone.

Primary comparison uses full-population click AUC; report all four AUC/Logloss, auxiliary mean, and inherited history slices with sample/positive/negative counts. Use fixed bins empty,1..16,17..64,>64; slice findings remain exploratory.
falsifiers: If both pair candidates fall below A111-0.00015, reject pair sufficiency in the tested fixed-seed implementation, even if one beats purchase-only. A positive I_CFB can motivate higher-order follow-up but does not prove gradient alignment.
If I_CFB is near zero or negative, do not claim all three task sources are required for positive superadditivity; report whether pair effects account for the grouped result.
If gains disappear under later paired-seed repeats or user-cluster uncertainty analysis, withdraw repeated-mechanism support. Same-seed replay is never counted as repeated support.

If source/config matching, common-state forward/moment equality, input masking, task-gradient ownership or frozen host checks fail, classify as execution/integrity failure before interpreting AUC. Do not silently change the protocol or reuse unmatched controls.
No new candidate exceeding incumbent means no new performance best. Exceeding source baselines alone does not prove useful compression/task complementarity or a new contribution.
alternative_explanations: Subset effects may reflect gradient count/magnitude, effective shared-context step size, sparse Adagrad history, correlated labels or dense clipping rather than task-specific directional cooperation. This factorial localizes source dependence but cannot isolate these alternatives; a later matched-magnitude control would require its own plan and budget.
Interactions can arise from nonlinear training trajectories and AUC rank aggregation. Positive interaction is not evidence of a particular event-level behavioral mechanism.
Long-history slice gains can reflect different label prevalence, sample composition or preexisting compression/normalization pathways. No new fields or timestamp information are available.

Adaptive reuse of a single validation set after many rounds and fixed-seed optimization noise can produce apparent winners. Withheld assessment remains closed; selection is provisional until repetitions and a frozen assessment suite.
Unselected task projections remain trained on detached context values; their forward capacity and BCE participation remain intact. This isolates shared embedding update ownership, not task removal.

Thus improved click ranking must not be described as universal four-task improvement. Report the full task table and loss tradeoffs.
